labels.notes: Not marked. The prefix-agnostic form of tools/ledger.py's docstring_label_re finds no bold backticked label anywhere in the file. The bold `**theo:syracuse_cycle.**` at l.15 has no backticks, so it is not a mark. The row is `partial`, as the dispatch requires. (1) theo_syracuse_cycle_printed_false negates the full printed statement: x : ℤ, 0 < n, T^[n] x = x, n the least period (the strongest reading of « n-cycle », so the refutation covers both readings), α n-periodic with α k = a_k(x), conclusion count ≠ 2. It does so in both index conventions. Witness −17, recomputed: orbit −17, −25, −37, −55, −41, −61, −91, −17; a = (1,1,1,2,1,1,4); 𝒟 ∩ ⟦1,7⟧ = {3,6}, or {4,7} in the β convention. It is not a strawman, but it rests on the reading a_i = a_i(x_0) of OQ-68 (a) (minor finding 1). (2) theo_syracuse_cycle_nonminimal_false: T(1) = 1 and a_0(1) = 2, so (1) read as a 2-cycle has 𝒟 ∩ ⟦1,2⟧ = {1,2}. This is legitimate: the paper itself separates « period n » (cor:ring_following_equivalent_enumerate, def:syracuse_cycle_period_denote) from « minimal period » (cor:ring_periodic_minimal_period). (3) theo_syracuse_cycle_of_cited (and _shift) adds x > 0, n the least period, TwoDescMatveev B and TwoDescCheck B. All four are disclosed (checklist l.43, l.54; REPORT hypotheses), and the first two are necessary by (1) and (2). TwoDescMatveev B mentions no cycle. It is the effective (P, n)-finiteness step in the proof of cor:property_defined_cycles_gcd (l.166), at the proved ε₀ = 1/2 − log₂3/4 and constant 2. It is true for large B by any Baker-type lower bound for 2^P − 3ⁿ (with theo:matveev as printed, 2^P/(eP)^d ≤ 2·2^{0.896P} bounds P), so it is not false. It cannot trivialise the theorem, being purely Diophantine. TwoDescCheck B is the finite check of l.326 (« check the finitely many remaining cases »), i.e. the conclusion restricted to p_n ≤ B. It is a finite statement for each B: n < P ≤ B, finitely many a-sequences, at most one cycle each. It is not false as far as I know (see notes). It does not assume the conclusion, because the cycles with p_n > B are handled only by the proved bound twoDesc_corollary_hyp through TwoDescMatveev. That is the paper's l.323–326 structure. Neither is an axiom. Both are Prop-valued defs taken as explicit arguments of the two assembly theorems, so the dispatch's constraint is met. (4) The adjacent case: twoDesc_bound, twoDesc_bound_pow_four, twoDesc_corollary_hyp and the conditional theorem carry no gap hypothesis at all. So every configuration is covered: k₂ = k₁ + 1, the wrap-around k₁ = 1, k₂ = n (δ₂ = 1), and n = 2. twoDesc_adjacent itself states only k₂ = k₁ + 1 in ⟦1, n⟧. The wrap-around case is the second conjunct of twoDesc_abs_le, |m| ≤ E(1, α₂, α₁). So « k₂ = k₁ + 1 closes through the bound » is true in the sense the REPORT gives it: it closes modulo the same two cited steps as the main case. twoDesc_adjacent's hypotheses are satisfiable (the cycle (1) as a 2-cycle: k₁ = 1, |2⁴ − 3²| = 7 ≤ E(1,1,1) = 7 ≤ 20). This is not witnessed in Lean, which is not required. Its first conjunct (no integer strictly between k₁ and k₁ + 1) is trivially true and decorative. (5) Non-vacuity: twoDesc_nonvacuous_seq17 instantiates twoDesc_delta_i at i = 4 and twoDesc_delta_j at j = 0 on seq17, twoDesc_key_classes, and twoDesc_abs_le on the real cycle (cycle_neg_seventeen). Values recomputed: Δ'_4 = 2780 = 2²·695, Δ'_0 = 1112 = 2³·139, A'_7 + (2¹¹ − 3⁷) = 2363 − 139 = 2224 = 2⁴·139, |2¹¹ − 3⁷| = 139 ≤ 139, 695.

findings.what: Findings 1 and 2 go to the author as « false over ℤ » and « n must be the least period, even for x > 0 ». Both rest on the reading a_i = a_i(x_0) = ν₂(3x_i + 1) of OQ-68 (a), which the checklist row for a_i (l.44) states but the finding sentences do not. Under the printed a_i := T^i(x_0) (l.271), 𝒟_Γ = {i : x_i > 1}. Then the cycle of −17 has 𝒟 = ∅, and (1) as a 2-cycle has 𝒟 = ∅, so neither witness refutes l.306. The refutations are correct in the reading taken, and that reading is the evident intent (the strict library refutes the literal one, literal_neg_one, literal_one). But a finding sent as a fact should name its reading. The T-syr-steiner audit made the same kind of wording point.

(2) E(3,1,3) = 139, E(4,3,1) = 695 = 5·139, E(4,1,3) = 305 = 5·61 (305 mod 139 = 27), E(3,3,1) = 253 = 11·23 (253 mod 139 = 114). (4) The displays at −17 in ℚ: l.311–312 at u = 0,1,2 gives 2224, 3336, 5004 = 2Δ'_u, and at u = 4,5 gives 11259, 33777/2. l.313–314 at u = 4,5 gives 5560, 8340 = 2Δ'_u, and at u = 0,1,2 gives 88960/81, 44480/27, 22240/9. Neither equals Δ'_u or Δ_u at any ascending u. (5) Random periodic sequences, 4000 configurations, n ∈ [2,12], 1 ≤ k₁ < k₂ ≤ n, α₁, α₂ ∈ [1,5], adjacent and n = 2 cases included. All hold with 0 failures: the key identity both ways round (A'_{k₂+1} + D = 2^{δ₂}E(δ₁,α₁,α₂), A'_{k₁+1} + D = 2^{δ₁}E(δ₂,α₂,α₁), P = α₁ + α₂ + n); the exact forms of Δ'_i, Δ_i at every k₁ < i < k₂ and of Δ'_j, Δ_j at every k₂ − n < j < k₁; display l.313 at i and display l.311 at j, each equal to 2Δ'. At −17, 139⁴ ≤ 16·12¹¹. ε₀ = 1/2 − log₂3/4 = 0.10376 > 0, against the paper's log₃2 − 1/2 = 0.13093. (2·2^{P(1−ε₀)})⁴ = 16·2^{2P}3^P = 16·12^P. p_n ≤ 2n on the cycles (1), (−1), (−5,−7) and (−17). (8) l.324, first inequality literally: at −17 the RHS is 3^{3.5}·16 + 16·2^{3.5} = 929.27 < 1112 = min Δ'_u over ascending u. Second inequality: the exponent gap is RHS − LHS = (1 − L/2)(n − P/L), L = log₂3, which is negative exactly when 3ⁿ < 2^P. In 47 959 pairs (n < 200, P < 400) with 3ⁿ < 2^P the first term alone exceeds the RHS every time. So the inequality needs n ≥ P log₃2, the reverse of the positive case, and the same holds for l.302 in theo:steiner_2.
notes: No major finding. Every claim in the REPORT was checked against the file, the paper or exact arithmetic, and each is true as stated: the ten paper findings, the planner's (a) and (b), the key identity, the true two-term and ∼_S forms, the bound and ε₀, the conditional theorem, the adjacent case and the non-vacuity. Observations for the master, none a defect. (i) TwoDescMatveev and TwoDescCheck are Prop-valued defs, the shape the hub uses for named externals. But they are not the cited theorems' statements (not theo:matveev, not cor:property_defined_cycles_gcd). They are this proof's two specific consequences at ε₀, the constant 2 and the bound B, taken as explicit arguments. At graduation they should not be listed as named externals without T-syr-cited's ruling, as the T-syr-steiner audit said of SteinerArithStmt. (ii) Context for T-syr-cited, from my own knowledge and not checked against a source in references/: a cycle with exactly two descending indices per least period is a « 2-cycle » in the sense of Simons (Math. Comp. 74 (2005), « On the nonexistence of 2-cycles for the 3x+1 problem »). The positive form of theo:syracuse_cycle is then a published theorem, and TwoDescCheck B should hold for every B. So the two hypotheses are jointly satisfiable and the conditional theorem is not vacuous. (iii) The bound for an empty gap is carried by twoDesc_bound and twoDesc_abs_le, not by twoDesc_adjacent alone (see the label notes). The REPORT's checklist row names all three, which is accurate. (iv) The Steiner and TwoDescents treatments of the cited steps differ: Steiner states neither and proves an equivalence, TwoDescents carries them as hypotheses as its dispatch asked. Both are within their dispatches, and harmonising them is the master's call. Probes were written under /tmp and deleted. No lake build was run. Nothing outside this AUDIT file was written.
